data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference is defensible via an evolutionary analogy where 'corroboration' signals survival fitness of the methodology, not the truth of the theory; this survives by costing Popper the idea of science converging on truth, reducing it to an adaptive process.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If evolutionary success is not correlated with truth-likeness (pessimistic meta-induction).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If this view reduces scientific rationality to mere biological adaptation, losing normative force.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the environment (nature) is not stable enough for selection to function as a reliable filter.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Drawing on evolutionary epistemology, the preference for corroborated theories is a meta-methodological rule that has itself survived severe tests (the survival of science).
